outcome: A December 2024 preprint by Yong-Geun Oh claimed a proof of the general Weinstein conjecture (and Arnold's chord conjecture) via contact instanton moduli theory; the author withdrew the claim in September 2025 after finding he could not rule out the associated Reeb orbit being constant, leaving the general conjecture open. No AI system was involved at any point.
summary: The Weinstein conjecture (does every regular compact contact-type level set of a Hamiltonian on a symplectic manifold carry a periodic Reeb orbit?) remains open in general since 26 January 2024. The one substantive event in the window is arXiv:2412.20731, 'Contact instantons and Proofs of Weinstein's conjecture and Arnold's chord conjecture,' submitted 30 December 2024 by Yong-Geun Oh, which claimed a full proof of the general Weinstein conjecture using contact-instanton moduli theory and Legendrianization of contactomorphisms. I opened both v1 and v2 of the arXiv entry. On 17 September 2025 the author posted v2 with a withdrawal comment reading (quoted verbatim from the arXiv comments field): 'It is still a possibility that the associated isospeed Reeb orbit could be a constant orbit which I cannot rule out at the moment. Sorry for the long delay realizing this.' This is a gap in a key step (ruling out a constant orbit), not a cosmetic fix, and the paper was never digested or accepted before the retraction, so the correct status is progress/incident under §6.1: an announced claim that was withdrawn, dated to the claim (since no resolution followed) rather than to the withdrawal — but per the instructions I recorded event.date as the withdrawal (2025-09-17) since that is the point at which the record can attest the claim did not stand; the claim itself (2024-12-30) predates the window's midpoint but is itself within the window and is the operative fact plus its retraction. No AI system, LLM, or automated proof assistant appears anywhere in the paper, its arXiv metadata, or any secondary coverage I found — Oh's argument is entirely traditional analytic/geometric contact-topology work. I separately checked the triage's flagged namesake, 'High dimension Weinstein conjecture and its application to Schiffer conjecture' (Zeitschrift für angewandte Mathematik und Physik, 2026): this is unambiguously a different 'Weinstein conjecture' — Payne's 1955 planar inequality Λ₁ ≥ λ₂ between the buckling and membrane eigenvalues, generalized to higher dimensions and applied to the Schiffer conjecture — with no connection to Reeb dynamics, contact geometry, or Hamiltonian flows. It is out of scope as a namesake, confirming the triage's read. I also checked arXiv:2508.01113 ('On the contact type conjecture for exact magnetic systems'), which invokes the (still-open) strong Weinstein conjecture as a hypothesis to build magnetic systems with prescribed contact-type properties, rather than proving any case of the Weinstein conjecture itself — also out of scope as a related-but-distinct problem. I checked the current Wikipedia 'Weinstein conjecture' article, which reports only the pre-2024 state (Taubes's 2007 dimension-3 proof) with nothing from 2024–2026. I checked the 'List of mathematical discoveries by artificial intelligence' Wikipedia page and it contains no mention of the Weinstein conjecture, contact geometry, or Reeb dynamics. A March 2025 survey ('A survey on the Weinstein conjecture,' Yanqiao Ding, Frontiers of Mathematics in China) exists but its full text is paywalled; the accessible abstract/reference list gave no indication of a new theorem proved after January 2024, and no mention of AI. I did not find any other proof attempt, partial result, or bound-moving paper on the general (higher-dimensional) Weinstein conjecture within the window.
competing_reading: One could argue the correct status is simply 'open' with no_change_found true, treating a withdrawn, never-verified preprint as not a 'happening' worth recording at all. I chose 'progress'/'incident' instead because §6.1 and §7 explicitly instruct that a withdrawn AI-adjacent-looking claim is itself an instructive event that must not be silently dropped, and because a serious, specific, later-retracted full-generality claim by an established expert in the field is exactly the kind of incident the schema is built to capture, even though in this case no AI was involved. The dating of event.date to the withdrawal rather than the original claim is also debatable; an argument could be made to date it 2024-12-30 (the claim) instead, since that is 'the claim' per §6.1's ai_role incident guidance for AI claims. I used the later date because it is the point at which the full story (claim + failure) is established, and because the instructions say 'dated to the claim' specifically for AI incidents, which this is not.
what_would_settle_it: A published errata/corrigendum from Oh explicitly stating whether the gap was later closed, or a new preprint (by Oh or others) building on or repairing the contact-instanton approach, would settle whether this remains a dead end or becomes a fresh claim. Access to the full text of Ding's March 2025 survey (currently paywalled) could also reveal whether any other 2024-2025 partial result exists that my searches missed.
